messages.subject: Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed()
parts:
Hello, 
I'm trying to reproduce the code of this article: https://www.r-bloggers.com/2019/11/spatial-data-analysis-with-inla/

When I reproduce the models (separately): 

m1 <- inla(Cases ~ 1 + AVGIDIST,
           data = as.data.frame(NY8),
           family = "poisson",
           E = NY8$Expected, control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
           control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE), verbose=TRUE)

m2 <- inla(Cases ~ 1 + AVGIDIST + f(ID, model = "iid"),
           data = as.data.frame(NY8), family = "poisson", 
           E = NY8$Expected,
           control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
           control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE), verbose=TRUE)

m.icar <- inla(Cases ~ 1 +  AVGIDIST + 
                 f(ID, model = "besag", graph = NY8.mat),
               data = as.data.frame(NY8), E = NY8$Expected, family ="poisson",
               control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
               control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE), verbose=TRUE)

m.bym = inla(Cases ~ 1 +  AVGIDIST + 
               f(ID, model = "bym", graph = NY8.mat),
             data = as.data.frame(NY8), E = NY8$Expected, family ="poisson",
             control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
             control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE), verbose=TRUE)

m.ler = inla(Cases ~ 1 +  AVGIDIST +
               f(ID, model = "generic1", Cmatrix = Cmatrix),
             data = as.data.frame(NY8), E = NY8$Expected, family ="poisson",
             control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
             control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE), verbose=TRUE)

I receive the same Error message:

poisson data are integers 0,1,2,3.... you intput 3.08... and that is an
error. well, earlier that was not checked for so this is why it had run
fine in earlier versions of the code (cannot recall when this happened)

the "xpoisson" will accept 'everything' and "poisson" accepts only
integers. its unclear what the interpretation of "xpoisson" really is.
